title: objectql: a committed trio handle reverts to unattributed instead of closed
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt

## What

After a `ScopedContext` trio transaction commits or rolls back, the engine drops the handle's owner record, so the handle reverts to "unattributed" instead of "closed". A late write that still carries that handle to another datasource is handed the dead foreign handle again.

A closed `transaction()` unit's handle is treated differently: `isClosedUnitHandle` answers true, the handle is treated as absent, and the late work runs unenrolled (#22855). The two kinds of handle should agree.

## Where

- `packages/objectql` trio owner record (the WeakMap keyed by handle that PR #35102 adds for route A of #35028), and the release on commit/rollback.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts` (`isClosedUnitHandle`, ~303-306) and `engine-execute-transactions.ts` (`enforceTransactionOrigin`).
- The PR #35102 test "forgets the owner once the trio commits" pins today's delivery.

## Origin

Nit N2 of contract review 6969574094 on PR #35102 (card #35028). It is the pre-PR behaviour for trio handles, unchanged by that PR and outside its card. The ADR-0119 note's "a handle the engine never opened" does not quite cover it.

## Suggested direction (unverified)

Mark the trio handle closed on commit/rollback (so `isClosedUnitHandle` answers true for it) instead of forgetting it, and pin that a late cross-datasource write carrying a committed trio handle runs unenrolled, as a closed `transaction()` unit's late work does.

Re-check: `git grep -n "isClosedUnitHandle" origin/main -- packages/objectql/src` and read the trio release path once #35102 has merged.
